Let $\Dh$ and $A$ be unital and separable $C^{*}$-algebras; let $\Dh$ be strongly self-absorbing. It is known that any two unital $^*$-homomorphisms from $\Dh$ to $A \otimes \Dh$ are approximately unitarily equivalent. As an application, we give a description of the Kasparov group $KK(\Dh, A\ot \Dh)$ in terms of $^*$-homomorphisms and asymptotic unitary equivalence. Along the way, we show that the Kasparov group $KK(\Dh, A\ot \Dh)$ is isomorphic to $K_0(A\ot \Dh)$.

Let \(\Dh\) and \(A\) be unital, separable \(C^{*}\)-algebras, and suppose that \(\Dh\) is strongly self-absorbing. It is known that any two unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms from \(\Dh\) to \(A \otimes \Dh\) are approximately unitarily equivalent. We show that, if \(\Dh\) is also \(K_{1}\)-injective, then they are in fact asymptotically unitarily equivalent. In particular, this implies that every unital endomorphism of \(\Dh\) is asymptotically inner.

Moreover, the automorphism group \(\Aut(\Dh)\), equipped with the point-norm topology, is compactly contractible in the sense that, for every compact Hausdorff space \(X\), the set of homotopy classes \([X,\Aut(\Dh)]\) consists of a single point. The corresponding statement also holds for the space of unital endomorphisms of \(\Dh\). As an application, we describe the Kasparov group \(KK(\Dh, A\otimes \Dh)\) in terms of \(^*\)-homomorphisms and asymptotic unitary equivalence. Along the way, we show that \(KK(\Dh, A\otimes \Dh)\) is isomorphic to \(K_{0}(A\otimes \Dh)\).

We prove that when \(\mathcal D\) additionally satisfies \(K_{1}\)-injectivity, this equivalence can be strengthened to asymptotic unitary equivalence. Consequently, every unital endomorphism of \(\mathcal D\) is asymptotically inner. We also establish that the automorphism group of \(\mathcal D\), equipped with the point-norm topology, is compactly contractible: for every compact Hausdorff space \(X\), the homotopy set \([X,\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)]\) consists of a single element. The analogous conclusion is valid for the space of unital endomorphisms of \(\mathcal D\). As a further application, we characterize the Kasparov group \(KK(\mathcal D, A\otimes \mathcal D)\) using \(^*\)-homomorphisms modulo asymptotic unitary equivalence. In the course of the argument, we also prove that \(KK(\mathcal D, A\otimes \mathcal D)\) is naturally isomorphic to \(K_{0}(A\otimes \mathcal D)\).

Let \(\mathcal{D}\) be a strongly self-absorbing unital separable \(C^*\)-algebra. A fundamental rigidity property of such algebras is that unital embeddings of \(\mathcal{D}\) into tensor products of the form \(A \otimes \mathcal{D}\) are essentially unique up to unitary perturbation. More precisely, any two unital \(*\)-homomorphisms
\[
\varphi, \psi : \mathcal{D} \longrightarrow A \otimes \mathcal{D}
\]
are approximately unitarily equivalent. This means that there exists a sequence of unitaries \((u_n)\) in \(A \otimes \mathcal{D}\) such that
\[
\lim_{n \to \infty} \|u_n \varphi(d) u_n^* - \psi(d)\| = 0
\]
for every \(d \in \mathcal{D}\). Thus, from the perspective of point-norm approximation, all unital copies of \(\mathcal{D}\) inside \(A \otimes \mathcal{D}\) look the same.

If, in addition, \(\mathcal{D}\) is \(K_1\)-injective, this uniqueness statement can be strengthened. In that case, the two unital \(*\)-homomorphisms are not merely approximately unitarily equivalent but asymptotically unitarily equivalent. That is, there exists a norm-continuous path of unitaries \((u_t)_{t \geq 0}\) in \(A \otimes \mathcal{D}\) such that
\[
\lim_{t \to \infty} \|u_t \varphi(d) u_t^* - \psi(d)\| = 0
\]
for every \(d \in \mathcal{D}\). The passage from approximate to asymptotic unitary equivalence is significant because it provides a continuous deformation implementing the equivalence, rather than merely a sequence of approximations.

One important consequence is that every unital endomorphism of \(\mathcal{D}\) is asymptotically inner. Indeed, applying the preceding result to two unital maps \(\mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}\), namely a given unital endomorphism and the identity map, shows that the endomorphism can be connected to the identity by an asymptotic path of inner automorphisms. Concretely, for any unital \(*\)-endomorphism \(\alpha : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{D}\), there is a norm-continuous path of unitaries \((u_t)_{t \geq 0}\) in \(\mathcal{D}\) such that
\[
\lim_{t \to \infty} \|u_t \alpha(d) u_t^* - d\| = 0
\]
for all \(d \in \mathcal{D}\). Thus, although \(\alpha\) need not itself be inner, it becomes inner in the asymptotic sense.

These uniqueness and deformation properties have strong topological consequences for the spaces of maps on \(\mathcal{D}\). In the point-norm topology, the automorphism group \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{D})\) is compactly contractible. The same is true for the space of unital endomorphisms of \(\mathcal{D}\). Compact contractibility means that every continuous map from a compact space into these mapping spaces can be contracted to a point through continuous maps. In particular, these spaces have a very flexible homotopy theory: compact families of automorphisms or unital endomorphisms can be continuously deformed to a constant family.

The paper also gives a description of Kasparov’s bivariant \(K\)-theory group
\[
KK(\mathcal{D}, A \otimes \mathcal{D})
\]
in terms of \(*\)-homomorphisms and asymptotic unitary equivalence. Under this description, classes in \(KK(\mathcal{D}, A \otimes \mathcal{D})\) may be represented by unital \(*\)-homomorphisms from \(\mathcal{D}\) into \(A \otimes \mathcal{D}\), with two such representatives identified when they are asymptotically unitarily equivalent. Moreover, this group is shown to be naturally isomorphic to
\[
K_0(A \otimes \mathcal{D}).
\]
Thus the bivariant theory with first variable \(\mathcal{D}\) collapses, in this setting, to ordinary \(K\)-theory of the \(\mathcal{D}\)-stabilized algebra \(A\). This reflects the strong self-absorption of \(\mathcal{D}\): tensoring with \(\mathcal{D}\) imposes a high degree of rigidity and uniqueness on the resulting \(C^*\)-algebraic structure.

The paper investigates the homotopy-theoretic and classification-theoretic consequences of strong self-absorption for unital separable C*-algebras. Let \(\mathcal D\) be a strongly self-absorbing C*-algebra which is \(K_1\)-injective, and let \(A\) be a unital separable C*-algebra. A central point of departure is the known fact that unital \(*\)-homomorphisms
\[
\mathcal D \longrightarrow A \otimes \mathcal D
\]
are approximately unitarily equivalent under suitable hypotheses. The paper strengthens this phenomenon by showing that such maps are not merely approximately unitarily equivalent, but asymptotically unitarily equivalent.

More precisely, the results show that any two unital \(*\)-homomorphisms from \(\mathcal D\) into \(A \otimes \mathcal D\) can be connected by a norm-continuous path of unitaries implementing equivalence in the limit. This upgrade from approximate to asymptotic unitary equivalence is significant because asymptotic equivalence carries stronger information and interacts more effectively with homotopy, \(KK\)-theory, and the topology of spaces of \(*\)-homomorphisms.

A key application concerns the structure of the endomorphism semigroup of \(\mathcal D\). The paper proves that every unital endomorphism of \(\mathcal D\) is asymptotically inner. In other words, if
\[
\varphi \colon \mathcal D \to \mathcal D
\]
is a unital \(*\)-endomorphism, then \(\varphi\) can be obtained as the pointwise limit of inner automorphisms along a continuous path of unitaries. Thus, from the asymptotic point of view, all unital endomorphisms of \(\mathcal D\) are indistinguishable from the identity map up to inner perturbation.

The paper also studies the topology of the automorphism group \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\) and of the space of unital endomorphisms of \(\mathcal D\). It proves that both spaces have strong contractibility properties. In particular, \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\) is compactly contractible, meaning that every continuous map from a compact space into \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\) can be contracted to a point through such maps. The same compact contractibility holds for the space of unital endomorphisms of \(\mathcal D\). These results show that, despite the possible algebraic richness of \(\mathcal D\), its automorphism and endomorphism spaces are topologically very flexible.

Finally, the paper connects these structural results with \(KK\)-theory. It gives a description of
\[
KK(\mathcal D, A \otimes \mathcal D)
\]
in terms of unital \(*\)-homomorphisms \(\mathcal D \to A \otimes \mathcal D\), modulo asymptotic unitary equivalence. Under this description, the \(KK\)-classes are represented concretely by \(*\)-homomorphisms, and two such representatives define the same class precisely when they are asymptotically unitarily equivalent. Moreover, the resulting group is naturally isomorphic to
\[
K_0(A \otimes \mathcal D).
\]
Thus the paper identifies a bridge between the classification of \(*\)-homomorphisms out of a strongly self-absorbing algebra, the topology of automorphism and endomorphism spaces, and the \(K\)-theoretic invariant \(K_0\).

counterfactuals.output:
We study structural and homotopical properties of strongly self-absorbing \(C^*\)-algebras through the asymptotic unitary equivalence of unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms. For a strongly self-absorbing algebra \(D\), we analyze when two unital embeddings into a \(D\)-absorbing \(C^*\)-algebra are connected by a norm-continuous path of unitaries, and relate this phenomenon to \(K_1\)-injectivity of \(D\). In particular, we show that \(K_1\)-injectivity provides a natural mechanism for upgrading approximate unitary equivalence to asymptotic unitary equivalence, yielding uniqueness results for unital \(D\)-absorbing maps and tensorial absorption isomorphisms.

We further investigate the topology of the automorphism group \(\operatorname{Aut}(D)\), showing that the strong self-absorption of \(D\) imposes strong contractibility and homotopy-rigidity properties on spaces of unital endomorphisms and isomorphisms. These results clarify the role of approximately inner half-flips and provide new connections between absorption, path-connectedness of unitary orbits, and the homotopy type of automorphism spaces.

As applications, we derive consequences for \(KK\)-theory and classification. We show that, under suitable \(K_1\)-injectivity hypotheses, unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms from strongly self-absorbing algebras are classified up to asymptotic unitary equivalence by their \(KK\)-classes in natural absorbing settings. This yields strengthened uniqueness theorems and provides tools for analyzing \(D\)-stable \(C^*\)-algebras, strongly self-absorbing tensor factors, and the interaction between homotopy-theoretic invariants and operator-algebraic absorption. The results contribute to a unified framework linking strongly self-absorbing \(C^*\)-algebras, automorphism group topology, and \(KK\)-theoretic classification.

The paper’s central theorem is a uniqueness result for maps out of a strongly self-absorbing \(C^*\)-algebra.

Let \(\mathcal D\) be a unital strongly self-absorbing \(C^*\)-algebra which is \(K_1\)-injective, and let \(A\) be a unital \(C^*\)-algebra. Then any two unital \(*\)-homomorphisms
\[
\varphi,\psi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow A\otimes \mathcal D
\]
are asymptotically unitarily equivalent. More precisely, there is a norm-continuous path of unitaries \((u_t)_{t\geq 0}\subset A\otimes \mathcal D\), often chosen with \(u_0=1\), such that
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\|u_t\varphi(d)u_t^*-\psi(d)\|=0
\qquad\text{for all }d\in \mathcal D .
\]
In particular, every unital map \(\mathcal D\to A\otimes \mathcal D\) is asymptotically unitarily equivalent to the canonical embedding
\[
d\mapsto 1_A\otimes d .
\]

The \(K_1\)-injectivity assumption is used to upgrade approximate unitary equivalences to controlled homotopies of unitaries, allowing one to build genuine asymptotic unitary paths.

Main consequences include:

1. **Uniqueness of \(\mathcal D\)-structure maps.**  
   If \(A\) is unital, then the choice of a unital embedding \(\mathcal D\to A\otimes \mathcal D\) is unique up to strong asymptotic unitary equivalence. Thus the \(\mathcal D\)-absorption structure on \(A\otimes \mathcal D\) is essentially canonical.

2. **Automorphisms of \(\mathcal D\).**  
   Taking \(A=\mathbb C\), any unital endomorphism of \(\mathcal D\), and in particular any automorphism
   \[
   \alpha\in \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D),
   \]
   is asymptotically unitarily equivalent to the identity map. Thus
   \[
   \alpha \sim_{\mathrm{asu}} \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D}.
   \]
   As a result, \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\) is path connected, and in fact the arguments imply much stronger homotopical triviality results: for \(K_1\)-injective strongly self-absorbing \(\mathcal D\), the automorphism group \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\), with the point-norm topology, is contractible.

3. **Consequences in \(KK\)-theory.**  
   Since asymptotically unitarily equivalent \(*\)-homomorphisms define the same \(KK\)-class, all unital maps
   \[
   \varphi:\mathcal D\to A\otimes \mathcal D
   \]
   determine the same class in
   \[
   KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes \mathcal D).
   \]
   Namely,
   \[
   [\varphi]_{KK}=[1_A\otimes \operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D}]_{KK}.
   \]
   In particular, every automorphism \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\) acts trivially in \(KK\)-theory:
   \[
   [\alpha]_{KK}=[\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D}]_{KK}.
   \]

Overall, the paper establishes a strong rigidity phenomenon: for \(K_1\)-injective strongly self-absorbing \(C^*\)-algebras, unital embeddings into \(\mathcal D\)-stable targets are unique up to asymptotic unitary equivalence, and this forces the automorphism group and the associated \(KK\)-classes to be homotopically and \(KK\)-theoretically trivial.

We prove that, for a \(K_{1}\)-injective strongly self-absorbing \(C^{*}\)-algebra \(\mathcal D\), approximate unitary equivalence of unital \(*\)-homomorphisms out of \(\mathcal D\) automatically upgrades to asymptotic unitary equivalence. More precisely, if \(A\) is a unital \(C^{*}\)-algebra and \(\varphi,\psi\colon \mathcal D\to A\) are unital \(*\)-homomorphisms which are approximately unitarily equivalent, then there exists a norm-continuous path of unitaries \((u_t)_{t\geq 0}\) in \(A\) such that  
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\|u_t\varphi(d)u_t^{*}-\psi(d)\|=0
\qquad(d\in\mathcal D).
\]
The \(K_{1}\)-injectivity assumption is used to remove the obstruction to connecting implementing unitaries by controlled homotopies.

As a consequence, the canonical approximately inner half-flip of \(\mathcal D\) is asymptotically inner, yielding strengthened uniqueness results for \(\mathcal D\)-absorbing maps and endomorphisms. We apply this to the topology of automorphism groups, showing that natural automorphism groups associated to \(\mathcal D\)-stable algebras have strong homotopical rigidity properties. In particular, the results imply contractibility phenomena for automorphism groups of stabilized strongly self-absorbing algebras and identify the relevant classifying spaces arising from \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D\otimes \mathbb K)\).

We also discuss consequences in Kasparov theory. The asymptotic uniqueness theorem gives canonical homotopies between Kasparov cycles induced by approximately unitarily equivalent \(\mathcal D\)-linear maps, leading to simplifications in the construction and comparison of \(KK\)-classes for \(\mathcal D\)-stable \(C^{*}\)-algebras. These applications clarify the role of \(K_{1}\)-injectivity in the structure theory of strongly self-absorbing \(C^{*}\)-algebras and provide a bridge between approximate intertwining techniques, homotopy theory of automorphism groups, and bivariant \(K\)-theory.

Let \(\mathcal D\) be a separable unital strongly self-absorbing \(C^*\)-algebra, i.e. \(\mathcal D\not\cong \mathbb C\) and the first-factor embedding
\[
\mathcal D\to \mathcal D\otimes \mathcal D,\qquad d\mapsto d\otimes 1
\]
is approximately unitarily equivalent to an isomorphism \(\mathcal D\cong \mathcal D\otimes\mathcal D\).

A central theorem of Dadarlat–Winter says, in one of its standard forms:

## Key theorem: uniqueness up to strong asymptotic unitary equivalence

Let \(A\) be a separable unital \(C^*\)-algebra. If
\[
\sigma,\gamma:\mathcal D\to A\otimes \mathcal D
\]
are unital \(*\)-homomorphisms, then \(\sigma\) and \(\gamma\) are strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent: there exists a norm-continuous path of unitaries
\[
(u_t)_{t\geq 0}\subset A\otimes \mathcal D,\qquad u_0=1,
\]
such that for every \(d\in \mathcal D\),
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\|u_t\sigma(d)u_t^*-\gamma(d)\|=0.
\]

Equivalently, the space of unital embeddings \(\mathcal D\to A\otimes\mathcal D\) is, up to homotopy/asymptotic unitary equivalence, essentially contractible.

---

## Application 1: asymptotic innerness of endomorphisms of \(\mathcal D\)

Taking \(A=\mathbb C\), any two unital \(*\)-homomorphisms
\[
\mathcal D\to \mathcal D
\]
are strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent. In particular, for every unital endomorphism
\[
\alpha:\mathcal D\to \mathcal D,
\]
there is a norm-continuous path of unitaries \((u_t)_{t\geq 0}\subset \mathcal D\), with \(u_0=1\), such that
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\|u_t\alpha(d)u_t^*-d\|=0
\qquad(d\in\mathcal D).
\]
Thus every unital endomorphism of \(\mathcal D\) is asymptotically inner, indeed strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent to \(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D}\).

---

## Application 2: compact contractibility of \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\)

The automorphism group \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\), equipped with the point-norm topology, is compactly contractible.

Concretely, if \(X\) is a compact Hausdorff space and
\[
f:X\to \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)
\]
is continuous, then \(f\) is null-homotopic. That is, there exists a continuous map
\[
H:X\times [0,1]\to \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)
\]
such that
\[
H(x,0)=f(x),\qquad H(x,1)=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D}
\]
for all \(x\in X\).

In particular, all homotopy groups of \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\) vanish:
\[
\pi_n(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D))=0,\qquad n\geq 0.
\]

---

## Application 3: computation of \(KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)\)

Let \(A\) be separable. The unital inclusion
\[
\iota:\mathbb C\to \mathcal D,\qquad \lambda\mapsto \lambda 1_{\mathcal D},
\]
induces an isomorphism
\[
\iota^*:KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)
\;\xrightarrow{\;\cong\;}\;
KK(\mathbb C,A\otimes\mathcal D).
\]
Since
\[
KK(\mathbb C,A\otimes\mathcal D)\cong K_0(A\otimes\mathcal D),
\]
one obtains the natural identification
\[
KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)\cong K_0(A\otimes\mathcal D).
\]

Under this identification, a class
\[
x\in KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)
\]
is determined by its value on the unit:
\[
x\longmapsto x([1_{\mathcal D}])\in K_0(A\otimes\mathcal D).
\]

In particular, for a unital \(*\)-homomorphism
\[
\varphi:\mathcal D\to A\otimes\mathcal D,
\]
its \(KK\)-class is determined by
\[
[\varphi(1_{\mathcal D})]=[1_{A\otimes\mathcal D}]
\in K_0(A\otimes\mathcal D).
\]

Thus the \(KK\)-theory of \(\mathcal D\) with coefficients in a \(\mathcal D\)-stable algebra is as simple as possible: it is just the \(K_0\)-group of the coefficient algebra.
